notes: A Lothian bus day ticket costs 5.50 GBP (via the app); the airport tram costs 7 GBP. Take the train to Stirling and Loch Lomond, and the 37 bus to Rosslyn. The city is hilly but walkable.
December brings Hogmanay (the New Year street party, with a torchlit procession on 30 December) and the Christmas market. Winter is 3-7°C, windy and rainy, and it gets dark by 15:30. May is ideal.
The castle costs 20 GBP and must be booked online. Museums (National, Galleries) are FREE. Pub lunch is 15-20 GBP, a whisky tasting 25 GBP; tip 10%.
Try haggis, Cullen skink, Scotch pie, cranachan and Irn-Bru. For whisky, Islay is smoky and Speyside is sweet.
The weather can turn through four seasons in an hour: bring a rain jacket and layers. The wind is harsh on Calton Hill and Arthur's Seat.
Harry Potter spots: Victoria Street, Greyfriars, the Elephant House and the Balmoral Hotel's Room 552.

stops.name: Edinburgh Castle
stops.tips: A castle on a volcanic rock: see the Scottish Crown Jewels, the Stone of Destiny and the 13:00 gun firing. Book a timed slot online (they sell out).

stops.name: Royal Mile
stops.tips: 1.6 km from the castle to Holyrood. Take in St Giles' Cathedral (Thistle Chapel), the closes (narrow alleys) and the Mary King's Close tour.

stops.name: Deacon Brodie's Tavern
stops.tips: Named after the thieving councillor who inspired Dr Jekyll. Try haggis, neeps and tatties.

stops.name: The Real Mary King's Close
stops.tips: 17th-century streets buried beneath the road above; plague history. Book ahead.

stops.name: The Scotch Whisky Experience
stops.tips: A barrel ride and a tasting, with a collection of 3,000 bottles. On Castlehill.

backups.name: Oink
backups.tips: Hog roast sandwiches; expect a queue.

backups.name: Camera Obscura
backups.tips: An illusion tower dating from 1835. An alternative to Mary King's Close, good with children.

stops.name: Arthur's Seat
stops.tips: An extinct volcano, 251 m high. 45 minutes from Holyrood Park, with panoramic views over the city and the Firth of Forth. It's windy.

stops.name: Palace of Holyroodhouse
stops.tips: The monarch's residence in Scotland. See Mary Queen of Scots' rooms and the ruined abbey.

stops.name: The Sheep Heid Inn
stops.tips: Said to be Scotland's oldest pub, dating from 1360 (royalty visited). It has a skittles alley and a village setting in Duddingston.

stops.name: Calton Hill
stops.tips: Home to the National Monument (an unfinished Parthenon) and the Nelson Monument. The best postcard view of the city, especially at sunset.

stops.name: Dean Village
stops.tips: A medieval mill village on the Water of Leith, a fairytale corner in the middle of the city.

backups.name: Dynamic Earth
backups.tips: A science centre telling the story of the planet. An alternative to Holyrood, good with children.

backups.name: Holyrood 9A
backups.tips: Burgers and craft beer, just below the Royal Mile.

stops.name: National Gallery of Scotland
stops.tips: Free, on the Mound. See Titian, Raeburn's The Skating Minister and Monarch of the Glen.

stops.name: Princes Street Gardens and Scott Monument
stops.tips: A Gothic rocket-shaped monument with 287 steps. The gardens have castle views and a floral clock.

stops.name: Stockbridge Market and Circus Lane
stops.tips: The market runs on Sundays. Circus Lane is a flower-lined back street, very Instagrammable.

stops.name: The Scran and Scallie
stops.tips: Tom Kitchin's gastropub in Stockbridge, serving Scottish ingredients.

stops.name: Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh
stops.tips: A botanic garden since 1670. The glasshouses are paid; Inverleith Hill has castle views.

backups.name: Scottish National Portrait Gallery
backups.tips: A neo-Gothic red building. Free entry, with portraits of Mary Stuart.

backups.name: The Pantry
backups.tips: Brunch in Stockbridge; expect a queue.

stops.name: Rosslyn Chapel
stops.tips: The 1446 chapel from The Da Vinci Code. See the Apprentice Pillar and hundreds of carvings. Take the 37 bus, 40 minutes.

stops.name: Roslin Glen
stops.tips: A walk through the stream valley below the chapel, with a ruined castle.

stops.name: The Original Rosslyn Inn
stops.tips: A village inn; lunch at the pub.

stops.name: Pentland Hills, Flotterstone
stops.tips: Winter hills. The Hillend artificial ski slope is an alternative.

backups.name: Craigmillar Castle
backups.tips: A ruined castle where Mary Stuart took refuge. Inside the city, an alternative to the Pentlands.

backups.name: Flotterstone Inn
backups.tips: A pub at the entrance to the Pentlands.

stops.name: Stirling Castle
stops.tips: 50 minutes by train. The castle of the Scottish kings, with the Great Hall and views of the Wallace Monument.

stops.name: National Wallace Monument
stops.tips: The 67 m tower tied to Braveheart and the 1297 Battle of Stirling Bridge. 246 steps.

stops.name: Stirling Old Town lunch
stops.tips: A café next to the Old Town Jail; try Cullen skink (smoked haddock soup).

stops.name: Balloch, Loch Lomond
stops.tips: The loch shore in winter. Luss village is reachable by car.

stops.name: Luss
stops.tips: A stone village on the loch shore. The pier at sunset (by tour or car).

backups.name: Doune Castle
backups.tips: The Monty Python and Outlander castle. An alternative to the Wallace Monument (by car).

backups.name: The Portcullis
backups.tips: A pub at the castle gate.

stops.name: Royal Yacht Britannia
stops.tips: The Queen's yacht from 1953 to 1997, moored at Ocean Terminal in Leith. Audio guide included.

stops.name: The Shore, Leith
stops.tips: The old harbour and Trainspotting's neighbourhood, with Michelin-starred restaurants.

stops.name: Fishers in Leith
stops.tips: Seafood in a harbour tower, open since 1991.

stops.name: Water of Leith Walkway
stops.tips: A 5 km riverside path from Leith to Dean Village, with Antony Gormley statues in the water.

stops.name: Surgeons' Hall Museums
stops.tips: A surgical museum covering the body snatchers Burke and Hare. Not for the faint-hearted.

backups.name: The Kitchin
backups.tips: Michelin-starred. Book the lunch menu ahead.

backups.name: Portobello Beach
backups.tips: A city beach with a Victorian promenade. An alternative to Leith.

stops.name: Greyfriars Kirkyard
stops.tips: Home to the Greyfriars Bobby dog statue. Harry Potter names appear on gravestones (Tom Riddle).

stops.name: The Elephant House
stops.tips: Breakfast at the café where Rowling wrote (reopened). The back room has castle views.

stops.name: National Museum of Scotland
stops.tips: See Dolly the sheep and the Lewis Chessmen. Free entry, with a rooftop terrace.

stops.name: Waverley Station
stops.tips: Take the tram to the airport, 35 minutes. Time to say goodbye.

backups.name: Mums Great Comfort Food
backups.tips: On Forrest Road; sausages and mash.

backups.name: Grassmarket
backups.tips: A Saturday farmers' and crafts market.
